clue.text: Blow out date once husband gets bitter?

parts.note: someone you once dated is an ex, a former partner
bitter is a type of beer, an ale

explanation.surface: A former partner is soured when a husband appears on the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a British pale beer, so it gives ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe air out of the lungs is to blow it out.

clue.text: Do relief work in Middle East, backed by employer

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: the employer is the boss

explanation.surface: An aid worker does relief work in the Middle East, with the backing of their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief here is the raised design of sculpture or metalwork, not humanitarian aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a design so it stands proud of the surface is producing relief work.

clue.text: Disable mast originally handling mobile phone

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word handling, its first letter
mobile means able to move about, so these letters shift into a new order

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A mobile phone mast is put out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like part of 'mobile phone' but signals the anagram of MAST plus H, giving HAMST.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting the tendon behind the knee cripples, so the verb means to disable or thwart.

clue.text: Team's one short after dead rubber

indicators.note: after places the team's letters behind the word for dead

parts.note: the late person is a dead one

indicators.note: one short means the team is missing a single member, so a letter goes

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A team is a player down for a match whose result no longer matters.
explanation.walkthrough: A dead rubber is a sports match played after the series is already decided; here rubber is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural rubber comes from the milky sap of the rubber tree.

clue.text: Lectures bearing fruit for speaker

indicators.note: for speaker means the words are as heard by a listener, judged by sound

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing; peaches are a fruit

explanation.surface: Talks that carry fruit, presented for the benefit of a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal talks given to an audience are lectures.

clue.text: Possessing minimal money, speaker's spent a tiny bit to get heard perhaps?

parts.note: spent and past both mean over and done

indicators.note: possessing means holding inside, so the small particle wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a particle is a tiny bit
the speaker refers to themself as I
P, penny, is the smallest coin

explanation.surface: A speaker who is nearly broke has used up a little to be listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard perhaps' is a grammatical definition: heard is a verb form of hear, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heard is the form of hear used after has or have, an example of this grammatical term.

clue.text: Caught up in flagrant drug taking in conclusion? On the contrary

indicators.note: taking in means swallowing something up, so one piece goes inside another
On the contrary swaps the roles, so the conclusion takes in the other pieces rather than the reverse

parts.note: the conclusion is the end
a flagrant offence is a gross one
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: Someone gets swept up in blatant drug-taking at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, GROSS + E would take in END; 'On the contrary' reverses this so END holds GROSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absorbed or wholly occupied by something is to be caught up in it.

clue.text: In desperation a homeowner raised capital

indicators.note: raised means sent upwards, which in a down entry reads the letters from bottom to top
In means the letters sit inside the run of words desperation a homeowner

explanation.surface: A desperate homeowner scrapes together some capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vietnamese capital city is an example of a capital.

clue.text: This rogue imbibes low energy drink

indicators.note: imbibes means drinks in, so one piece is taken inside the other
rogue means behaving unpredictably, so the letters of This go out of order

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rogue drinks a low-energy beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' makes STHI from This, and MOO goes inside after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A blended fruit beverage is a type of drink.

clue.text: Well, studying role playing is very dull

parts.note: well and so are both interjections opening a sentence

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the letters of studying role are rearranged

explanation.surface: Learning lines for a part is tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that crushes the spirit through tedium is extremely dull.

clue.text: Self-important politician in bar promises to pay

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar as in except, the same as but
MP is a Member of Parliament
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A pompous politician in a pub runs up a tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means except, giving BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pushy and full of their own importance is self-important.

clue.text: Absurd sentimentality about place down under

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: goo is gushing sentimentality
NZ, New Zealand, is a country down under

explanation.surface: Mawkish sentiment about Australasia is ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre or crazily outlandish describes something absurd.

clue.text: Person partaking of shorts regularly?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so alternate letters of shorts are taken

explanation.surface: Someone who often drinks small measures of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorts are small measures of spirits, and someone drinking them regularly is a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drunkard is someone who regularly drinks spirits.

clue.text: Musician needs axes to cut this? No, wrong

parts.note: x and y are the axes of a graph
to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: wrong means not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician has to take axes to something, then thinks better of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a percussion instrument with wooden bars is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Tabloids principally publish a lot of lies?

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the first letter of Tabloids is used

parts.note: to issue a magazine is to publish it

explanation.surface: Tabloids mainly print a great deal of untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on the phrase 'a tissue of lies'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tissue of lies is a whole interwoven web of falsehoods.

clue.text: Positioned in seat, fly and fly

indicators.note: positioned in means placed inside, so one piece is set within the other

parts.note: a saddle is a seat for a rider
a ked, or sheep ked, is a wingless parasitic fly

explanation.surface: A fly lands on a seat and then flies away.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'fly' is the insect, the second the verb meaning flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off in a hurry is to flee or fly.

clue.text: He scored runs batting, eclipsed by Australian mostly

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: eclipsed by means hidden inside, so one piece is swallowed by another
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Ossie is a variant spelling of Aussie
a cricketer who is batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricketer piled up runs but was outshone by an Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He scored' suggests the cricketer, but means a man who wrote music. 'mostly' drops the final letter of the Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer wrote opera scores, so he scored music.

clue.text: Expert supports popular euphemism for swearword that's not to be uttered

indicators.note: in a down entry, supports means placed underneath the earlier letters

parts.note: something in fashion is in
eff is a polite stand-in for a four-letter word
an able person is expert

explanation.surface: A specialist backs a well-liked polite substitute for a swearword.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too great or sacred to be expressed in words cannot be spoken.

clue.text: Pub's to exclude one caught being uncouth

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to bar is to exclude
one is I in Roman numerals
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pub bans someone who was caught behaving crudely.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, wild and uncivilised behaviour is uncouth.

clue.text: After a month workers finally get increase

indicators.note: after means the workers come behind the month

parts.note: Aug is short for August, a month
men are workers

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of get

explanation.surface: After a month the staff at last get a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To make larger or add to is to increase.

clue.text: Where Pict will be depicted? Certainly!

definitions.meaning: in the word depicted, Pict sits inside the letters D, E, E, D, a deed

explanation.surface: A question about where an ancient Briton might be portrayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Picts were an ancient people of Scotland; 'depicted' is DE-PICT-ED, Pict within a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic interjection agreeing strongly, like truly or certainly.

clue.text: Clergyman's art satisfying one's curiosity?

parts.note: a clergyman is, in archaic speech, one who 'pryest', thou art prying, which sounds like his title

explanation.surface: A clergyman's craft is to indulge his inquisitiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old second-person form of be: thou art prying, thou pryest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian minister ordained to perform rites is a clergyman.

clue.text: Fan's first to actually see advertisement for US showman

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter of actually

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
a bill is a poster, an advertisement

explanation.surface: An enthusiast is the first to actually notice a promotional poster.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cody ran a Wild West show that toured America and Europe.

clue.text: Soldier's in the cooler — he trained criminals

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the cooler

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is locked up in prison by a man who coached crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cooler' looks like slang for prison but means a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Oliver Twist, this character teaches a gang of boys to pick pockets.

clue.text: This beer is great right to the end

indicators.note: right to the end means the letter for right moves to the last position

parts.note: large means great in size

explanation.surface: A beer that is excellent all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to the end' looks like 'throughout' but moves R in LARGE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A light bottom-fermented beer is a type of beer.

clue.text: Pelt fellow with egg? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word for egg is kept

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Pelting a man with eggs? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb about throwing eggs, but is the noun, an animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hairy skin or coat is its pelt.

clue.text: Severe cold that's minus Fahrenheit

indicators.note: minus means take away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: frigid means very cold

explanation.surface: A harsh chill below zero on the Fahrenheit scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and unbending, as in harsh discipline, is severe.

clue.text: Complex libel cases allowed less time? That's hard to understand

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so one piece is put around another
complex means intricate, so the letters of libel are jumbled
less means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: legit means legitimate, allowed

explanation.surface: Complicated libel trials have been given less time in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' reads as lawsuits but means encloses; 'Complex' scrambles libel to ILBLE, and 'less' drops the time letter from the word for allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting that cannot be read is hard to make out or understand.

clue.text: Come together to chat — that's good for son

indicators.note: good for son means the letter for good replaces the letter for son

parts.note: to converse is to chat

explanation.surface: A meeting where people chat, and that's good for the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet at a single point is to come together.

clue.text: Burning forest's temperature

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A forest's temperature rises in a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and fervent feeling is figuratively burning.
